Definition: n. The act of slipping away from a place secretly and without saying good-bye to anyone. "It's getting late," Rob whispered to Janet. "Let's take French leave and get out of here."
n. A name used informally for the average man. Let us say that Joe Doakes goes to the movies three times a year. Compare: MAN IN THE STREET, SO-AND-SO.
n. A name used informally for the average citizen. It is John Q. Public's duty to vote at each election. Compare: JOE DOAKES.

n. , informal Police unit trained for especially hazardous or sensitive law-enforcement assignments; short for Special Weapons and Tactics. Joe made the SWAT team of the NYPD due to his athletic skills.
v. phr. , informal To believe in one's ability, purpose, or power to perform or succeed. Be confident; be positive; tell yourself you are the greatest; above all, think big!
n. A sudden change of course or a decision opposite to what was decided earlier. Her decision to become an actress instead of a dentist was an about face from her original plans.
n. phr. Finally, but later than it should have been; at last. Mother said, "It's about time you got up, Mary." The basketball team won last night. About time.
adv. phr. Of first or highest importance; most especially. Children need many things, but above all they need love. Synonym: FIRST AND LAST.
n. , slang A regular user of LSD on whom the hallucinogenic drug has left a visible effect. The reason John acts so funny is that he is a regular acid head.
n. , slang A characteristic kind of rock in which loudness and beat predominate over melody; especially such music as influenced by drug experiences. John is a regular acid rock freak.
v. To have a good effect on, suit. The meat loaf did not agree with him. The warm, sunny climate agreed with him, and he soon grew strong and healthy.
prep. , informal Crowded with; filled with. The lake was alive with fish. The stores were alive with people the Saturday before Christmas.
n. , slang 1. A stray cat. 2. A person (usually a female) of rather easy-going, or actually loose sexual morals; a promiscuous person. You'll have no problem dating her; she's a regular alley cat.
v. To provide for; leave room for; give a chance to; permit. She cut the skirt four inches longer to allow for a wide hem. Democracy allows for many differences of opinion.
n. A brain wave, 8-12 cycles per second, associated with a state of relaxation and meditation and, hence, free of anxieties. Try to produce some alpha waves; you will instantly feel a lot better.
v. Signify; add up to. John's total income didn't amount to more than a few hundred dollars.
n. , slang Phencyclidine, an addictive hallucinatory narcotic drug extremely dangerous to the users' health, also called PCP. Mike has gone from grass to angel dust; he will end up in the morgue.
adv. phr. Generally; customarily. As a rule, the boss arrives at the office about 10 A.M.
adv. phr. Unanimously; together; involving all. The audience arose as one man to applaud the great pianist.
prep. Regarding; concerning; about. You needn't worry as regards the cost of the operation. He was always secretive as regards his family.
adj. phr. Held by an anchor from floating away; anchored. The ship rode at anchor in the harbor.
n. A sudden increase in the birth rate. The universities were filled to capacity due to the baby boom that followed World War II.
n. A small grand piano no longer than three feet, maximally four feet. This apartment can't take a regular grand piano, so we'll have to buy a baby grand.
v. To act to avoid or lessen one's involvement in something; draw or turn back; retreat. The townspeople backed away from the building plan when they found out how much it would cost.
n. , slang , citizen's band radio jargon Rear of vehicle. I am watching your back door.
n. , informal A person or animal that is always fighting, quarreling, or doing bad things. The boy was a bad actor and nobody liked him.
n. , slang 1. A check for which there are no funds in the bank. 2. Counterfeit paper money. Why are you so mad? I was paid with some bad paper.
n. , slang , also informal The entire matter at hand; the whole situation; the entire contest. You said we can get a second mortgage for the house?! Wow! That's a whole new ball game.
n. , slang Flattery that is an obvious exaggeration; statements that are obviously made with an ulterior motive. Cut out the banana oil; flattery will get you nowhere!
v. phr. To be a couple; belong to one another. No one is surprised to see them together anymore; if is generally recognized that they are an item.
v. phr. To be strict or critical with another; be severe. "Don't be so hard on Jimmy," Tom said. "He is bound to rebel as he gets older."
v. To act naturally; act normally without trying unduly to impress others. Just try being yourself; I promise people will like you more.
v. phr. To intend to do; to plan to commit. The police felt that the gang may be out to rob another store.
v. phr. To be determined about something. Tow is set upon leaving his Chicago job for Tokyo, Japan, although he speaks only English.
v. phr. To yield results. We hope that the company's new investment policy will bear fruit.
n. , slang , citizen's band radio jargon A police radar unit designed to catch speeders. Watch the bear trap at exit 101.
v. phr. To follow the rhythm of a piece of music by moving one's fingers or feet. Jack was beating time with his foot during the concert, which annoyed his neighbor.
prep. On account of; by reason of; as a result of. The train arrived late because of the snowstorm.
v. phr. To happen to; befall. What will become of the children, now that both parents are in jail?
v. phr. To complain about something. Stop beefing about your job, Jack. You could have done a lot worse!
adv. phr. As a preliminary statement; in the first place. To begin with, you are far too young to get married.
v. To constantly complain. Jim is always bellyaching about the amount of work he is required to do.
adj. or adv. Below standard. Bob was fired because his work has been below par for several months now. Antonym: UP TO PAR or UP TO SNUFF.
n. A large jail or prison. The rapist will spend many years in the big house.
n. , slang A major scandal; a big upheaval. I'll raise a big stink if they fire me.
n. A day of great unhappiness; a disaster. It was a black day when our business venture collapsed.
n. An engagement or date arranged by friends for people who have not previously known one another. A blind date can be a huge success, or a big disappointment.
v. phr. To suddenly say something even if one was not planning to do so, or if it was not expected of them. "My brother Bob is in jail," Tony blurted out, before anybody could stop him.
n. , informal A great disappointment; a bitter failure. When he failed to get on the team it came as a body blow to him.
v. phr. To reach the lowest point (said chiefly of economic cycles). According to the leading economic indicators the recession will bottom out within the next two months.
adj. phr. On the way to; going to. I am bound for the country club. The ship is bound for Liverpool.
n. A sudden insight; a stroke of comprehension. Listen to me, I've just had a major brainstorm, and I think I found the solution to our problem.
v. phr. To liberate oneself from someone or something. Jane tried to break loose from her attacker, but he was too strong.
v. phr. To take down and pack tents and camping things; take your things from a camping place. The scouts broke camp at dawn.
v. phr. , slang , informal To walk into a place casually (like a soft blowing wind). Betsie breezed in and sat down at the bar.
v. To throw a baseball pitch close to. The pitcher threw a high inside pitch to brush the batter back. Synonym: DUST OFF.
n. , slang An unusually long, thin radio antenna on a car that bends back like a whip when the car moves fast. He's very impressed with himself ever since he got a buggy whip.
v. phr. To burn to the ground; be totally gutted by fire. The old frame house burned down before the firefighters could get to it.
v. phr. 1. To enter suddenly. Stuart burst into the room, screaming angrily. 2. To break out. The crowd burst out cheering when the astronauts paraded along Fifth Avenue.
v. To approach a person in order to speak with him or her in private. After waiting for several hours, Sam managed to buttonhole his boss just as she was about to leave the building.
adv. phr. As a result of choosing because of wanting to; freely. John helped his father by choice. Mary ate a plum, but not by choice. Her mother told her she must eat it.
adv. phr. As the result of a mistake; through error. He picked up the wrong hat by mistake.
v. phr. To become quiet; relax. "Calm down, Mr. Smith," the doctor said with a reassuring smile. "You are going to live a long time."
n. A crop grown to be sold. Cotton is a cash crop in the South. They raise potatoes to eat, but tobacco is their cash crop.
v. , informal To see (a chance) and profit by it; take advantage of (an opportunity or happening). Mr. Brown cashed in on people's great interest in camping and sold three hundred tents.
n. , slang Something very wonderful, special, or good. John's new hike is really the cat's meow. Mary's party is going to be the cat's pajamas.
v. To give a military command ordering soldiers to stop shooting. "Cease fire!" the captain cried, and the shooting stopped.
n. A period of negotiated nonaggression, when the warring parties involved promise not to attack. Unfortunately, the cease-fire in Bosnia was broken many times by all parties concerned.
n. A group of convicts or slaves in the old South who were chained together. Chain gangs are no longer an acceptable way of punishment, according to modem criminologists.
v. phr. To be willing to risk an action whose outcome is uncertain. "Should we take the boat out in such stormy weather?" Jim asked. "We can chance it," Tony replied. "We have enough experience."
n. , slang A small, suburban house built by a land developer available at low cost and resembling the other houses around it. They moved to a suburb, but their house is just a cheesebox.

adj. Definite; well defined. The president's new policy of aggressive action is a clear-cut departure from his old methods of unilateral appeasement.

Definition: Een bonusuitkering aan de aandeelhouders in de vorm van aandelen uit de agioreserve.
Een optie is at-the-money als de uitoefenprijs (vrijwel) gelijk is aan de actuele koers van de onderliggende waarde. At-the-money series worden gewoonlijk het meest actief verhandeld.
Kleinste verandering bij de notering van een obligatierendement. Eén basispunt is 0,01%. Als het rendement van een obligatie van 7,25% naar 7,30% stijgt, dan neemt het toe met 5 basispunten.
Vergoeding die een bank aan haar klanten berekent voor het in bewaring houden en administreren van effecten.
Biedprijs. De prijs die door de 'markt' wordt geboden voor de aankoop een bepaald effect.
Het afgeven van prijzen waartegen men effecten wil kopen. Het tegenovergestelde van laten.
Engelse term voor een topaandeel of hoofdfonds. Voorbeelden van Nederlandse blue chips zijn onder andere Koninklijke Olie, Philips, ABN AMRO en Ahold.
Een verhandelbaar recht om op een bepaald moment in de toekomst een afgesproken hoeveelheid onderliggende waarde te kopen tegen een vooraf afgesproken prijs.

Effecten zonder dividend- of couponblad. Eventueel dividend wordt door het Centrum voor Fondsenadministratie uitbetaald aan banken en commissionairs. Deze zorgen vervolgens voor de uitbetaling van het dividend aan de aandeelhouders.
Deel van een obligatie waarop zich een aantal coupons bevindt.
Het ophouden te bestaan (expireren) van een optie. Een optie heeft altijd een beperkte looptijd, na het bereiken van de einddatum (expiratiedatum) bestaat de optie niet meer.
Administratiecode die wordt toegekend aan aandelen.
Markt voor korte termijnkrediet met een looptijd van minder dan een jaar.

Een optie op het edelmetaal goud. Amsterdam Exchanges noteert goudopties met een onderliggende waarde van 10 troy ounce goud per contract. Een troy ounce is 31,1035 gram. Goudopties zijn Europese stijl.

Een uitgevende instelling kan aan het begeleidende syndicaat een optie verstrekken om een aantal extra aandelen uit te geven tegen de uitgifteprijs. Hierdoor kan bij grote belangstelling voor het aandeel een ongewenste koersbeweging worden voorkomen.
Een beursgenoteerde onderneming waarvan een belangrijke groei en uitbreiding wordt verwacht. Voorbeelden van groeifondsen zijn bijvoorbeeld ondernemingen in de internet- en biotechnologiesector.
Een optiecontract met als onderliggende waarde een index zoals de AEX-index, de Amsterdam Midkap-index of de FTSE's Stars-index.
International Security IdentificatioN code. Internationale administratiecode die aan een aandelenfonds wordt toegekend.
(Fysieke) effecten die bestaan uit mantel, talon en dividendbewijzen of coupons. K-stukken staat voor klassieke stukken. Fysieke effecten worden in toenemende mate vervangen door Global Note s.
De prijs die 'de markt' wil ontvangen voor de verkoop van een bepaald effect.
Het (gedwongen) afbouwen van een positie. Dit kan door een clearingorganisatie, bank of commissionair worden afgedwongen als een belegger bijvoorbeeld niet aan zijn margin-verplichtingen kan voldoen.

Een order om zo snel mogelijk effecten te kopen of te verkopen zonder een limiet, dus zonder maximumprijs voor een kooporder of zonder minimumprijs voor een verkooporder. Ook wel bestensorder genoemd.
Een koers van 100% van de nominale waarde.
Winst behaald op geïnvesteerd vermogen. Als een belegger € 100 rente ontvangt over een tegoed van € 1000 dan bedraagt het rendement op zijn belegging 10%.
In Brussel gevestigde overkoepelende organisatie die protocollen opstelt voor het internationale financiële (data)verkeer.
Het verkrijgen van een shortpositie in een optie door een openingsverkoop.
Een belegger die een shortpositie in opties verkrijgt door het doen van een openingsverkoop.
De laatste koers van een effect op een handelsdag.
Aandelen geven aan de eigenaar ervan stemrecht tijdens de Algemene Vergadering van Aandeelhouders. Houders van certificaten van aandelen hebben geen stemrecht.
Tijdelijk samenwerkingsverband van twee of meer handelsbanken bij een introductie of een vervolgemissie. Een van de deelnemende syndicaatsleden treedt op als syndicaatsleider of lead-manager.
Het gebruik maken van het kooprecht bij een calloptie en het verkooprecht bij een putoptie.

Letterlijk groothandel. Op de effectenbeurs van Amsterdam Exchanges wordt een onderscheid gemaakt tussen retail- en wholesalehandel. Als wholesale gelden effectentransacties boven een bepaald volume. Deze volumegrens kan per fonds verschillen.

Obligaties die onder de nominale waarde worden uitgegeven en geen rente uitkeren. Op de aflossingsdatum wordt de nominale waarde uitgekeerd, het verschil tussen uitgifteprijs en nominale waarde is het rendement.

A round bar hinged to a karabiner or rappel rack used for abseiling .
A dendritic system of underground streams or passages wherein branches join successively to form a major stream or passage .
Fall of rock from roof or wall of a cave.
Very small speleothems consisting of short stalks with bulbous ends, usually occurring in numbers in patches.
Clay, silt, fine sand and/or humus deposited in a cave.
Transported materials such as silt, clay, sand and gravel which cover the bedrock floor or partially or wholly block some part of a cave.
A smooth, polished and rounded speleothem found in shallow hollows into which water drips. Internally has concentric layers around a nucleus.
Ascending or descending by means of opposed body and/or limb pressures against two facing walls.
A rock wedged between two fixed rock surfaces.
An instrument for measuring vertical angles or anglesof dip .
Karst , usually tropical, dominated by its projecting residual relief rather than by its closed depressions.
The "splash cups" that form on certain cave floors beneath energetic ceiling drip sites.
Fossilized large excrement of animals, sometimes found in caves, especially those used as lairs.
A scavenger which feeds on animal dung, including guano .
The wearing away of bedrock or loose sediment by mechanical action of moving agents, especially water. i.e. Corrosion and abraison
A length of rope used as a safety when crossing a rebelay . CRAWL (WAY) A passage which must be negotiated on hands and knees. Cf. flattener .
The assemblage of small terrestrial animals found living in darkness beneath stones, logs, bark, etc. Potential colonizers of caves.
The part of a cave which daylight does not reach.
A cave without streams or drips of water.
Cave features due to secondary mineral precipitation,usually of calcite . Syn. speleothem .
A mechanical device for descending ropes.
A deposit formed from drops falling from cave roofs or walls, usually of calcite .
A valley without a surface stream channel.
A speleothem of abnormal shape or attitude. Cf. helictite .
A spring fed only by percolation water .
A cave developed along a fault or fault zone, either by movement of the fault or by preferential solution along it.
A passage , which, though wide, is so low that movement is only possible in a prone position.
A deposit formed from thin films or trickles of water over floors or walls, usually of calcite . Cf. travertine .
Where a rope or ladder hangs vertically and free of the walls.
The direction of a north-south grid line on a map. Except for the north-south grid line through the point of origin of the grid , it will differ slightly from true north .
A semi-cylindrical, elongate recess in a cave surface, often meandering or anastomosing .
A speleothem , which at one or more stages of its growth changes its axis from the vertical to give a curving or angular form.
A steel or other alloy, oval- or D-shaped link with a spring-loaded gate on one side to admit a rope or to clip to a ladder , piton , etc.

A cave in a lava flow; usually a tube or tunnel formed by flow of liquid lava through a solidified mass, or by roofing of an open channel of flowing lava. Small caves in lava also form as gas blisters.
A colourless water tracer , which fluoresces blue.
A sedimentary rock consisting mainly of calcium carbonate, CaC03.
A cave containing a stream or active speleothems .
Miniature rimstone dams with associated tiny pools of the order of 1cm wide and deep on flowstone .
A scavenger feeding on animal carcasses (not prey).
A rechargeable alkaline battery for use with an electric cap lamp.
Assigning an alphanumeric index to a cave entrance.
A kind of stalactite which has been partly submerged and the submerged part covered with dog-tooth spar to give the appearance of a drumstick.
An animal association found in water separating grains of sand or fine gravel.
Ascent on a rope using prusik knots or ascenders .
A red organic dye which gives a red fluorescence to water. Detectable in very dilute solutions so used in water tracing and dye gauging .
Thin speleothem on cave precipitated from water films exuding from pores or cracks.
A scavenger feeding on decaying organic material.
(1) Referring to rock with water-filled voids. (2) Referring to water which has dissolved as much limestone or other karst rock as it can under normal conditions.
An animal that eats dead remains and wastes of other animals and plants (cf. coprophage, necrophage, saprophage ).
A cave that has been made accessible to the public for guided visits.
A cave feature formed erosionally or by weathering in cave enlargement such as current markings or rock pendants .
The exploration, description and scientific study of caves and related phenomena.
A secondary mineral deposit formed in caves, most commonly calcite .
A shallow cavity in the top of a stalagmite .
A complex of irregular, inter-connecting cavities intricately perforating the rock. The cavities may range from a few centimetres to more than a metre across.
A speleothem hanging downwards from a roof or wall, of cylindrical or conical form, usually with a central hollow tube.
A speleothem projecting vertically upwards from a cave floor and formed by precipitation from drips.
A steep-sided valley in karst , generally short, ending abruptly upstream where a stream emerges or formerly did so.

A speleothem projecting upwards from a cave floor in the form of a calcite ridge. A medial crack appears along the top of the ridge where water is thought to be forced from the speleothem under capillary action.
Suture in rock formed where pressure solution has taken place, often leaving a thin lamina of insoluble material along it.
A hole in rock in a streambed eroded by eddying water, with or without sand or pebble tools.
Conekarst in which the residual hills have very steep to overhanging lower slopes. There my be alluvial plains between the towers and flat-floored depressions within them.
Compact calcium carbonate deposit, often banded, precipitated from spring , river or lake water. Cf. tufa.
A cavernicole unable to live outside the cave environment.
A cavernicole which spends only part of its life cycle in caves and returns periodically to the epigean domain for food.
The direction of the geographical north pole at a place.
The surface between phreatic water which completely fills voids in the rock, and ground air, which partially fills higher voids.
A place where a cave roof dips under water but lifts above it farther on. Cf. duck (-under) .
A descender consisting of an aluminium block with slots, knobs and a safety gate.

Form of kundalini yoga advanced by Astara, Inc. (see "Astara's healing science"), for: "attunement" to the "etheric part" of oneself, expansion of consciousness, personal healing, and "psychic unfoldment."
Form of aura balancing whose theory posits a "Higher Self," "spiritual guides," and healthful "Universal Principles" that "live" within each human.
Quasicabalistic method that involves numerology and magical applications of sound.
Placement of needles into the scalp over parts of the brain that supposedly control various body functions.

Ayurvedic "treatment" in which warm sesame oil, or a warm "herbal oil," streams onto the forehead of a recumbent person. Its purported design is to purify the "mind-body" and relax the nervous system.
Variation of psychic healing practiced by Niall Gerrard, an Irishman and a former student of "metamorphic techniques" (see "metamorphic technique").
Variety of bodywork "therapies" native to Thailand. Their purported design is to create "energetic balance" and "wholeness" of body, mind, and spirit in practitioners and their clients.
The treatment of illness by sea air and sea water. It encompasses sea bathing, ocean voyaging, and sojourning at seaside resorts.
A component of VortexHealing. It is a purported fast technique that can be a form of absent healing and allegedly works with the "energetic blueprint" of problems.
Ancient Chinese exercise system of Taoist origin. Purportedly, the Waitankung exercises allow one's "inner energy" (chi) to fill the body like an electric current.
Group of Healing Tao practices according to whose theory the brain is connectible to "Universal knowledge."
Combination of yoga and Zen Shiatsu developed by Alessandro Cantelli, reportedly as a "self-treatment method" for balancing "meridians." The name "Yotsu" derives from the expression "Yogic Shiatsu."
Combination of shiatsu and other oriental techniques, developed by Shizuto Masunaga, the originator of Zen Shiatsu. Zen Tantra is an antecedent variation of Bodywork Tantra.
(French) Each menu item is priced separately: Foods prepared to order.
(French) Refers to ice cream on top of pie.
(French) To give a dish a more appetizing appearance by garnishing it.
Capellini ("Fine Hairs") A thin, delicate pasta. These strands are best if used with thinner, delicate sauces. Other uses: break in half and put in soup; use in salads or stir-fry meals.

A white, powdery thickener finer than flour. It is quite expensive and preferable to cornstarch because it provides a clear finish. Its extracted from rhizomes. It was originally used by American Indians to heal arrow wounds, hence the name 'arrowroot'.
(French) To top food with cheese or bread crumbs, then baked.
Small, boat shaped pastry tarts made of short crust pastry or puff pastry, baked blind and then filled with sweet or savory fillings.
(French) Sauce derived from Hollandaise, with a tarragon reduction added.
Milled rice is white, but the outer bran layer can be brown, red or black. In the case of black rice, the raw grains look charred and the cooked ones are the color of blackberries.
To bake a pie crust without the filling. Metal weights or dried beans are usually used to keep the pastry from bubbling.
An ice cream soda made with vanilla ice cream and root beer.
(Bread Pudding) Toasted bread topped with caramelized-sugar corn syrup, sliced longhorn cheese, raisins and cinnamon, and baked until cheese melts.

Originally, paper thin slices of raw beef with a creamy sauce, invented at Harry's Bar in Venice. In recent years, the term has come to describe very thinly sliced vegeatables, raw or smoked meats, and fish.
Blue corn meal much thicker than atole. Served with red chile with pork or spareribs in place of potatoes or rice.
French for 'made from rags.' In cooking it refers to a small chopped pile of thin strips of an ingredient. Usually it is raw, but sometimes sauteed. Mostly used to garnish.

A white, powdery thickener finer than flour. It is extracted from the starch endosperm of wheat or corn. It must be dissolved in a cold liquid before it is added to a hot mixture or it will lump. It results in a glazy, opaque finish.
Rolled or flat corn tortillas topped or stuffed with meat, cheese, onions, and red or green chile sauce.
A mother sauce. Basic brown sauce.
Long, flat pasta meaning "Small Ribbons". Perfect for heavier sauces, like cheese, meat and tomato sauces. For variety, try breaking in half and putting in soups, or use for a salad.
A pungent, salty liquid made from fresh anchovies that is essential in Thai cooking.
a raspberry liqueur with a high alcohol content
A moist dough of ground, dried corn that has been soaked in limewater, then cooked. Used in tamales.
A delicate wafer cookie, honey-combed and fan-shaped, made on an oblong iron. It is typically served as a garnish atop ice creams.
Avacado salad served as a dip or on lettuce as a salad, or ingredient in many other dishes.
(Cream Candy) Condensed milk used as a spread or ice cream topping.
Also called tiger lily bids or golden needles, dried day lily buds that are nutritious and sweet. They are used often in Chinese dishes.
This large, tubular pasta literally means "Small Muffs". Stuff Manicotti with a mixture of meat, cheese and vegetables, top with your favorite sauce, and bake. Or stuff and freeze for a later time.
A soft unripened cheese originally from Neufchatel-en-Bray, France. It has a fat content of 44-48%. Philadelphia sells it as low-fat cream cheese in the U.S..
Crisp Indian wafers made of legume flour or both rice and legume flours. They are usually served with drinks or as a snack with such accompaniements as chopped onions, tomatoes, coriander, and chili.
To cook partially by boiling for a short period of time.
Brown, unrefined cane sugar found in cone-shaped pieces used to sweeten coffee and desserts.
Also known as pignolias and pinon. The pine nut is the seed of the stone pine. They have a creamy look and a light 'pine' taste. They are used often in Italian, Spanish, and Middle Eastern cooking.
Thin decoratively patterned Italian wafer cookies that are made in an iron similar to a waffle iron. They may be flat or rolled into ice cream cones.
The Italian word for ham, used in the names of raw hams coming from Italy, in particular Proscuitto di Parma and Proscuitto di San Daniele.
Literally means "Radiators". This ruffled, ridged shape adds elegant interest to any sauce. It also works well baked in casseroles, or used in salads and soups.
Sugar that hasn't been refined enough to achieve a granulated quality. It looks like coffee crystals. This coarse sugar is harder to dissolve, making it a nice choice for sprinkling on foods.
A crystalline form of salt that is mixed with cracked ice to freeze ice cream.
An aromatic liquid made by distilling rose petals. It is used often in Middle Eastern pastries and can be found in many Middle-eastern groceries.
Cloth bag filled with select herbs used to season soups or stocks.
Sugar molded into a cone shape, with the base traditionally wrapped in blue paper. Nowadays its mainly manufactured for export to Arab countries.
Known as nasi ketan. Glutinous rice that cooks up stick and sweet. The unhulled rice is black and turns purplish black when cooked. The hulled rice is white.
Small, green, firm, tomatoes. They are covered with a paper like husk that's removed before cooking. Their acid flavor add a great flavor for sauces.

Mexican pancakes that are either made of flour or masa harina (ground corn). They make an excellent foundation for all sorts of fillings. Enchiladas are softened tortillas that are filled and rolled. Tacos are fried tortillas.
A common garden weed served as a leafy vegetable. Also called purslane.

The oil extracted from the walnut. It can be quite expensive and goes rancid quicker than most oils. However, it gives most foods a wonderful nutty flavor whether you cook with or drizzle it. Use it on greens, pasta, or vegetables.
Bain marie in French. A method of gently cooking delicate foods such as custards, on the stove or in the oven in a pan partially fillled with water.
An Italian custard like dessert made solely of egg yolks, sugar, and (traditionally) Marsala wine.
A material that has a pH of 7.0 or higher (an alkaline), since acids can weaken cellulose in paper, cloth, and board and lead to embrittlement" (Griset and Kodack 1999:155).

The process of evaluating a collection for the purpose of documenting its condition, relating it to the mission and goals of the repository, and determining courses of action regarding its care and management.
Transfer of property to an institution under the terms of a deceased person's will.
A chemical used to strengthen the structural material of an object.
Small scale, minute cracking of a material (similar to crazing). In glass, it results from the leaching out of alkalis.
The act of physically removing an object from a repository's collection.
A granular substance which has high moisture absorbing and emitting properties. It is often used as a moisture stabilizer in packing, storing, and exhibiting items that are sensitive to humidity.
A passive insect or rodent trap that uses an adhesive to trap the pest.
See Oil Painting page, Mediums, Varnishes, and Solvents
This is a combination of gum arabic and silica formed into a jelly-like substance to give an impasto look to watercolors. Not to be confused with Oleopasto.
Mannequin. Used to study and draw from when a model is not possible. There are lay figures of people and of some animals, such as horses.

A wooden stick of various length, usually about 2 feet, with a wooden or cloth ball at one end. The end is put on a dry section of the painting and the stick is used as a support, upon which the brush hand can be rested to steady the brush.
See Oil Painting page , Mediums, Varnishes, and Solvents
The American trade name for the paint pigment known as phthalocyanne blue and green .
The American trade name used to denote the pigment called quinacridone red when it is of the scarlet or yellowish shade.
A psychological phenomenon with a force-like character which is evident in our acting or trying to act and is necessary for these types of events. Chris Eliasmith
Capability of some digital video equipment to automatically adjust input video timing to match a reference video input. Eliminates the need for manual timing adjustments.
A digital tape recording format developed by Sony which uses a constrained version of MPEG-2 compression at the 4:2:2 profile, Main Level (422P@ML) using 1/2-inch tape cassettes.
The total amount of bits available on the media being used. In DVD, the bit budget of a single sided/single layer DVD5 disk is actually 4.7 GB.
The number of levels that a pixel might have, such as 256 with an 8-bit depth or 1,024 with a 10-bit depth.
Transmission of digital video a bit at a time down a single conductor such as coaxial cable. May also be sent through fiber optics. This standard is covered under ITU-R BT.656 (CCIR 656).
A continuous series of bits transmitted on a line.
A nonlinear editing term for the location of individual audio/video clips (or scenes). Also known as a clip bin.

A fixed deviation from proper clock phase that commonly appears in D1 digital video equipment. Some digital distribution amplifiers handle improperly phased clocks by reclocking the output to fall within D1 specifications.

A digital representation of a component analog signal set, most often Y, B-Y, R-Y. The encoding parameters are specified by ITU-R BT.601-2 (CCIR 601). The parallel interface is specified by ITU-R BT.656 (CCIR 656) and SMPTE 125M.
A digitally encoded video signal, such as NTSC or PAL video, that includes horizontal and vertical synchronizing information.
Digital video picture defect caused quantizing at too coarse a level.
A high definition digital component format based on D9. Records on 1/2-inch tape with 100 Mbps video.

This variant of DV uses a video data rate of 100 Mbps--four times that of other DV systems--and is aimed at the high definition EFP end of the market. Eight audio channels are supported. The format is similar to D9 HD.
The actual program (audio, video and/or data) without metadata. See also: Metadata.

A 625-line video standard that allows processing of component video quality digital signals by composite PAL equipment. The signal can be distributed and recorded in a composite digital form using D2 or D3 VTRs.

Short for interlaced scanning. Also called line interlace. A system of video scanning whereby the odd- and even-numbered lines of a picture are transmitted consecutively as two separate interleaved fields. Interlace is a form of compression.
Also referred to as Studio MPEG, Professional MPEG and 442P@ML. Sony's Betacam SX is based on MPEG 4:2:2. See: MPEG-2.

1. Data flow from single source to mutiple destinations; a multicast may be distinguished from a broadcast in that number of destinations may be limited. 2. Aterm often used incorrectly to describe digital television program multiplexing.
A term used by network designers to describe network links that have many possible endpoints.

A term used for editing and the storage of audio, video and data. Information (footage) is available anywhere on the media (computer disk or laser disc) almost immediately without having to locate the desired information in a time linear format.
A project aimed at obtaining a new generation of set-top boxes that are interoperable. These new devices will enable a new range of interactive services to be provided to cable customers.
The process of converting the voltage level of a signal into digital data before or after the signal has been sampled.
Popular software for streaming audio and video over the Internet. made by RealNetworks of Seattle, Washington.
Popular software for streaming audio and video over the Internet. made by RealNetworks of Seattle, Washington.
The process of clocking digital data with a regenerated clock.
A device that converts parallel digital information to serial.
The SMPTE standard for standard definition serial digital component and composite interfaces.
The SMPTE standard for formatting AES/EBU audio and auxiliary data into digital video ancillary data space.
The SMPTE standard for bit-serial digital interface for high-definition television systems.
The SMPTE standard defining the data representation of the 720x483 progressive signal at 59.94 Hz.
The SMPTE standard defining the serial interfaces for both 4:2:2P (progressive) on two-SMPTE 259M links and 4:2:0P (progressive) on a single SMPTE 259M link (at 360Mbps).
The SMPTE standard for 24-bit digital audio format for HDTV bit-serial interface. Allows eight embedded AES/EBU audio channel pairs.
The SMPTE standard for Serial Digital Transport Interface (SDTI).

The SMPTE standard for synchronous serial interface (SSI) for MPEG-2 digital transport streams; used as the "standard" for the output from the ATSC systems multiplexer and the input to DTV transmitters.
A RAID system implemented by low level software in the host system instead of a dedicated RAID controller. While saving on hardware, operation consumes some of the host's power. See also: RAID .
The process of converting a file or program from one formator resolution to another.

Term given to picture displays that have a wider aspect ratio than normal. For example, TV's normal aspect ratio is 4:3 and widescreen is 16:9. Although this is the aspect ratio used by HDTV, widescreen is also used with normal definition systems.
The separation of a roll of camera original negative into its individual scenes.
A record sheet giving details of the scenes photographed on a roll of original negative.
The base ('Celluloid') surface of a strip of film.
A test method for determining the optimum print requirements for a variable area sound track.
The audio equivalent of the video dissolve where one sound track is gradually faded out while a second sound track simultaneously replaces the original one
The amount of data that a particular connection can sustain over time. Usually measured in bytes/second.
The process of taking analog video information from a camera or deck and turning it into digital information that can be used by a computer.
LEVEL SYNC-EVEN SYNC. The relation between the picture and sound records during editing, when they are in alignment and not offset as for projection.
A digital device designed to store and display a single television frame as a "freeze frame." (See also Still Store.)
General terms for all production and preparation work up to the Answer Print stage before Release Printing.
A freeware program used to rip DVDs
A rotatable ring on the lens of a camera that allows for manual focusing. Ideally, you want a focus ring with distance markings so that you can
When speaking of video or film recording, the number of frames per second that are recorded (and then played back).
sending information from one program to another
A high-speed serial interface that can be used to attach DV cameras, storage devices, printers, or networks to a computer.
Describes a scene or program which has been completed. Also, "that's a wrap."
Different types of “keys” can be used to remove the background from a video clip to expose underlying video. See chroma key and luminance key.
A set of professional lights, light stands and lighting accessories, usually contained in a heavy-duty carrying case.
The end point of an edit.
The most common composite video signal used in Europe. It has a frame rate of 25 fps.
The telecine transfer relationship of film frames to video fields. Film shot at 24 fps is transferred to 30 fps NTSC video with an alternating two-field/three-field relationship.
A filter that enables the rotation of clip frames around any of three axes, the positioning of a frame in any of three dimensions and the control of the point of view through perspective adjustments.
A lens filter which polarizes the light coming into the lens. Can be used to increase saturation and to eliminate reflections in glass or water.
A special streaming video and audio architecture created by Real, Inc.
An optical printing effect eliminating selected frames of the original scene to speed up the action.

A single lens reflex camera. Unlike a camera with a separate viewfinder, in a SLR camera, you acutally look through the lens at your subject. A 35mm still camera with removable lenses is typically an SLR.
A frame numbering system adopted by SMPTE that assigns a number to each frame of video which indicates hours, minutes. seconds and frames (e.g., 01:42:13:26).
A camera that uses three separate CCDs to gather separate red, green, and blue data.
Trade name of a high-quality special effects system similar in application to a chromakey switcher. Electronic implementation of the "blue screen" used for motion picture special effects.
Reducing height and width of the picture on a video monitor so that the edges, and thus portions of the blanking, can be observed.
Portions of VITC and LTC reserved for recording information of the user's choosing, e.g., Keykode numbers, footage count, etc.
"Burned-in windows," usually on a video workprint, displaying Keykode numbers and time code, footage count, audio time code, scene, take, etc. (May also be burned in.)
In a motion picture studio or processing laboratory, a rough print of a motion picture film used for editing and study of action and continuity.
Also called S-video (short for separate video), Y/C video has separate luma (Y) and chroma (C) video signals. (See also component video and composite video.)
Similar to a focus ring, but used for manually zooming the camera.
Recording audio over an existing video program without affecting the video images.
Transition that produces the effect of displaying an incoming clip as alternating bands that eventually cover the outgoing clip.
The position of a cut relative to an overlying transition.
A complete video image consisting of two fields of video per frame.
The SMPTE time code defining the end of a clip. The frame with this time code is not included in the clip.
An editing process where both outgoing and incoming clips are trimmed at a cut point to shorten one while lengthening the other to maintain the overall length of a program.
L-cut or J-cut. Adjusting synchronized audio or video clips so that one starts slightly before or after the other.
A mode of appearance for EditDV Unplugged’s Project window. The text view contains names, descriptions, and numbers of clips stored in the Project window bins.
The graphic representation of a program displayed in the Sequencer window.

To see agate in a dream, signifies a slight advancement in business affairs.
Alms will bring evil if given or taken unwillingly. Otherwise, a good dream.
For a young woman to dream of an alms-house, denotes she will meet failure in her efforts to contract a worldly marriage.
To dream of catching fish is good. If you fail to catch any, it will be bad for you.
To dream of visiting Asia is assurance of change, but no material benefits from fortune will follow.
Conditions will change from good to bad if you are joined with others in back-biting. For your friends to back-bite you, indicates worriment by servants and children.

To dream that you have a bass voice, denotes you will detect some discrepancy in your business, brought about by the deceit of some one in your employ. For the lover, this foretells estrangements and quarrels.
To dream of seeing them on your person, denotes poverty and small ills. To kill them is good.
To dream of being beheaded, overwhelming defeat or failure in some undertaking will soon follow. To see others beheaded, if accompanied by a large flow of blood, death and exile are portended.
Eating or baking them, indicates ill health and family peace ruptured over silly disputes.
To dream of blackberries denotes many ills. To gather them is unlucky. Eating them denotes losses.
To dream of seeing trees and shrubs in blossom, denotes a time of pleasing prosperity is nearing you.
To dream of bomb shells, foretells anger and disputes, ending in law suits. Many displeasing incidents follow this dream.
Hearing an ass bray, is significant of unwelcome tidings or intrusions.
To dream of being in a brothel, denotes you will encounter disgrace through your material indulgence.
To dream of a cameo brooch, denotes some sad occurrence will soon claim your attention.
To dream of seeing a chair maker, denotes that worry from apparently pleasant labor will confront you.
For a woman to dream of a chemise, denotes she will hear unfavorable gossip about herself.
To dream of a city hall, denotes contentions and threatened law suits. To a young woman this dream is a foreboding of unhappy estrangement from her lover by her failure to keep virtue inviolate.
To dream of seeing your coat-of-arms, is a dream of ill luck. You will never possess a title.
This dream denotes that foes will bring disastrous suits against you. Beware of titles.
To dream of cocoa, denotes you will cultivate distasteful friends for your own advancement and pleasure.
To dream of coke, denotes affliction and discord will enter your near future.
To see coke ovens burning, foretells some unexpected good fortune will result from failure in some enterprise.
To see in your dreams a composing stick, foretells that difficult problems will disclose themselves, and you will be at great trouble to meet them.
To dream of copper, denotes oppression from those above you in station.
To dream of a coppersmith, denotes small returns for labor, but withal contentment.

To dream of a cotton gin, foretells you will make some advancement toward fortune which will be very pleasing and satisfactory. To see a broken or dilapidated gin, signifies misfortune and trouble will overthrow success.
To dream of a counselor, you are likely to be possessed of some ability yourself, and you will usually prefer your own judgment to that of others. Be guarded in executing your ideas of right.
To dream of a cut, denotes sickness or the treachery of a friend will frustrate your cheerfulness.
Dairy is a good dream both to the married and unmarried. See Churning Butter.
To be delayed in a dream, warns you of the scheming of enemies to prevent your progress.
Derricks seen in a dream, indicate strife and obstruction in your way to success.
To see or use a draw-knife, portends unfulfiled hopes or desires. Some fair prospect will loom before you, only to go down in mistake and disappointment.
To see an engineer, forebodes weary journeys but joyful reunions.
Envelopes seen in a dream, omens news of a sorrowful cast.
To dream of a fiddle, foretells harmony in the home and many joyful occasions abroad. See Violin.
To dream of a fire budget, denotes disagreement over small matters.
To dream of fishhooks, denotes that you have opportunities to make for yourself a fortune and an honorable name if you rightly apply them.
To see flax in a dream, prosperous enterprises are denoted.
To dream of a foal, indicates new undertakings in which you will be rather fortunate.

For a young woman to dream of forsaking her home or friend, denotes that she will have troubles in love, as her estimate of her lover will decrease with acquaintance and association. See Abandoned and Lover.
To dream of the future, is a prognostic of careful reckoning and avoiding of detrimental extravagance.
To dream of gaiters, foretells pleasant amusements and rivalries.
To dream of being caught in a gale, signifies business losses and troubles for working people.
To dream that you see any one afflicted with gangrene, foretells the death of a parent or near relative.
To see a gas lamp, denotes progress and pleasant surroundings. To see one explode, or out of order other wise, foretells you are threatened with unseasonable distress.
To dream of gasoline, denotes you have a competency coming to you through a struggling source.
To dream of gems, foretells a happy fate both in love and business affairs. See Jewelry.
To dream of gold leaves, signifies a flattering future is before you.
To hear the sound of a gong while dreaming, denotes false alarm of illness, or loss will vex you excessively.
To dream of distributing handbills over the country, is a sign of contentions and possible lawsuits. If you dream of printing handbills, you will hear unfavorable news.
To dream of possessing bright new harness, you will soon prepare for a pleasant journey.
To dream of seeing a helmet, denotes threatened misery and loss will be avoided by wise action.
To see hemp seed in dreams, denotes the near approach of a deep and continued friendship. To the business man, is shown favorable opportunity for money-making.
To dream of hens, denotes pleasant family reunions with added members. See Chickens.
To dream of the hide of an animal, denotes profit and permanent employment.
To dream of a hook, foretells unhappy obligations will be assumed by you.

To dream of implements, denotes unsatisfactory means of accomplishing some work. If the implements are broken, you will be threatened with death or serious illness of relatives or friends, or failure n business.
To dream of indigestion, indicates unhealthy and gloomy surroundings.
Empty ink-stands denote that you will narrowly escape public denunciation for some supposed injustice. To see them filled with ink, if you are not cautious, enemies will succeed in calumniation.
To dream of an interpreter, denotes you will undertake affairs which will fail in profit.
To dream of this month, denotes you will be afflicted with unloved companions or children.
To dream of a jester, foretells you will ignore important things in looking after silly affairs.
To dream of a Jew's-harp, foretells you will experience a slight improvement in your affairs. To play one, is a sign that you will fall in love with a stranger.
To dream that you feel joy over any event, denotes harmony among friends.
To dream of using a knocker, foretells you will be forced to ask aid and counsel of others.
To dream of seeing a leak in anything, is usually significant of loss and vexations.
To dream of a lime-kiln, foretells the immediate future holds no favor for speculations in love or business
To dream of eating limes, foretells continued sickness and adverse straits.
To dream of seeing a mantilla, denotes an unwise enterprise which will bring you into unfavorable notice.
To dream of a large manufactory, denotes unusual activity in business circles. See Factory.
To dream of seeing marigolds, denotes contentment with frugality should be your aim.
To dream of May bugs, denotes an ill-tempered companion where a congenial one was expected.
To dream of meadows, predicts happy reunions under bright promises of future prosperity.
To dream you see or pass a mile-post, foretells that you will be assailed by doubtful fears in business or love. To see one down, portends accidents are threatening to give disorder to your affairs.

To see mulberries in your dreams, denotes that sickness will prevent you from obtaining your desires, and you will be called upon often to relieve suffering. To eat them, signifies bitter disappointments.
To dream of musk, foretells unexpected occasions of joy, and lovers will agree and cease to be unfaithful.
To dream of water mussels, denotes small fortune, but contentment and domestic enjoyment.
To dream of noodles, denotes an abnormal appetite and desires. There is little good in this dream.
To dream of nutmegs, is a sign of prosperity, and pleasant journeyings.
o dream of obligating yourself in any incident, denotes that you will be fretted and
To dream of this order, signifies that you will have sincere friends, and misfortune will touch you but lightly. To join this order, foretells that you will win distinction and conjugal bliss.

For a woman to dream that she sees a man wearing over-alls, she will be deceived as to the real character of her lover. If a wife, she will be deceived in her husband's frequent absence, and the real cause will create suspicions of his fidelity.
To see a pine tree in a dream, foretells unvarying success in any undertaking. Dead pine, for a woman, represents bereavement and cares.
To dream of your pocket, is a sign of evil demonstrations against you.
To see ponies in your dreams, signifies moderate speculations will be rewarded with success.
To see a poor-house in your dream, denotes you have unfaithful friends, who will care for you only as they can use your money and belongings.
To dream of a post-office, is a sign of unpleasant tidings. and ill luck generally.
To see a prize fight in your dreams, denotes your affairs will give you trouble in controlling them.
To dream of a raccoon, denotes you are being deceived by the friendly appearance of enemies.
To dream of having ringworms appear on you, you will have a slight illness, and some exasperating difficulty in the near future. To see them on others, beggars and appeals for charity will beset you.
To see or eat roast in a dream, is an omen of domestic infelicity and secret treachery.
To dream of rubbish, denotes that you will badly manage your affairs.
To dream of salve, denotes you will prosper under adverse circumstances and convert enemies into friends.
To dream of sand, is indicative of famine and losses.
To dream of sapphire, is ominous of fortunate gain, and to woman, a wise selection in a lover.
To dream of sawdust, signifies that grievous mistakes will cause you distress and quarreling in your home.

To see any one with a scaldhead in your dreams, there will be uneasiness felt over the sickness or absence of some one near to you. If you dream that your own head is thus afflicted, you are in danger of personal illness or accidents.
To dream of being scalded, portends that distressing incidents will blot out pleasurable anticipations.
To dream of scum, signifies disappointment will be experienced by you over social defeats.
To dream of seed, foretells increasing prosperity, though present indications appear unfavorable.
To dream of a sentry, denotes that you will have kind protectors, and your life will be smoothly conducted.
To dream of sewing on new garments, foretells that domestic peace will crown your wishes.
To see sheet iron in your dream, denotes you are unfortunately listening to the admonition of others. To walk on it, signifies distasteful engagements.
To dream that you have sold anything, denotes that unfavorable business will worry you.
To dream of a sorcerer, foretells your ambitions will undergo strange disappointments and change.
To see spider-webs, denotes pleasant associations and fortunate ventures.
To dream of spleen, denotes that you will have a misunderstanding with some party who will injure you.
To dream that you are looking through a spy-glass, denotes that changes will soon occur to your disadvantage. To see a broken or imperfect one, foretells unhappy dissensions and loss of friends.
To dream of squalls, foretells disappointing business and unhappiness.
To dream of a stall, denotes impossible results from some enterprise will be expected by you.
To dream of a step-sister, denotes you will have unavoidable care and annoyance upon you.
To dream of a storage battery, opportune speculations will return you handsome gains.
To dream of struggling, foretells that you will encounter serious difficulties, but if you gain the victory in your struggle, you will also surmount present obstacles.
To dream of sugar-tongs, foretells that disagreeable tidings of wrong-doings will be received by you.
Sweet oil in dreams, implies considerate treatment will be withheld from you in some unfortunate occurrence.
To dream of a sybil, foretells that you will enjoy assignations and other demoralizing pleasures.
To dream of tallow, forebodes that your possessions of love and wealth will quickly vanish.
To dream you see a tapeworm, or have one, denotes disagreeable prospects for health or for pleasure.

To dream of a urinal, disorder will predominate in your home.

To dream of a waif, denotes personal difficulties, and especial ill-luck in business.
To dream of weevils, portends loss in trade and falseness in love.

To dream of a whip, signifies unhappy dissensions and unfortunate and formidable friendships.

To dream of a wine-glass, foretells that a disappointment will affect you seriously, as you will fail to see anything pleasing until shocked into the realization of trouble.
To dream that you are in a workhouse denotes that some event will work you harm and loss. See Prison.
To dream of a yard stick, foretells much anxiety will possess you, though your affairs assume unusual activity.
To dream of the zenith, foretells elaborate prosperity, and your choice of suitors will be successful.

An interaction of two or more chemicals that results in an effect greater than the sum of their separate effects.
The runoff of irrigation water from the lower end of an irrigated field.
Adjusting, negating, or removing pollution control equipment on a motor vehicle.
Dikes built along the contour of sloping farm land that hold runoff and sediment to reduce erosion.
Chemical that causes adverse health effects in domestic water supplies and is toxic to fresh water and marine aquatic life.
The dose level at which a substance produces a toxic effect.
An incinerator test in which emissions are monitored for the presence of specific organic compounds, particulates, and hydrogen chloride.
The continuous or intermittent flow of wastes into an incinerator.

The spent or used water from a home, community, farm, or industry that contains dissolved or suspended matter.Water Pollution: The presence in water of enough harmful or objectionable material to damage the water's quality.
An excavation where the intended use is for location, acquisition, development, or artificial recharge of ground water.
Area containing one or more wells that produce usable amounts of water or oil.
A watertight, gastight seal installed in a bore hole or well to prevent movement of fluids.
A hollow vertical tube, rod, or pipe terminating in a perforated pointed shoe and fitted with a fine-mesh screen.
Any biotum displaced from its normal habitat; a chemical foreign to a biological system.
The part of solid waste composed of grass clippings, leaves, twigs, branches, and other garden refuse.
Iron oxide flocculant (clumps of solids in waste or water); usually observed as orange-yellow deposits in surface streams with excess iron content. (See: floc , flocculation .)
A foreign substance or protein that, when introduced into the body, is recognised by the immune system.
Breathing difficulty caused by narrowing of the air passages that is reversible.
(B lymphocytes) White blood cells derived from stem cells in bone marrow and elsewhere that produce antibodies.
A type of white blood cell that contributes to inflammatory reactions and symptoms of allergy.
The most abundant of the carotenoids. b-Carotene has strong provitamin A activity. Unlike vitamin A itself, b-carotene is a strong antioxidant.
A carotenoid pigment found in a biological system.
The range of values within which a variable is likely to lie.
The generalisability of a study's findings to persons other than the study subjects.
Compounds that carry out only some of the functions of fat in foods.
Compounds that can replace conventional fat in foods and carry out all of the same functions.
Organic acids with a hydrocarbon chain of varying length; constituents of triglycerides and related lipids.
Foods that have been subjected to processing involving the action of yeasts or bacteria.
A method of dietary assessment in which subjects records the foods that they consume.
A company-defined target considered necessary to comply with a food safety objective.
The smallest sequence of a DNA molecule capable of directing protein synthesis or performing a regulatory function.
Inherited; a genetic disease is one that is inherited via a faulty gene.
To split a chemical compound into its constituents by the addition of water. Hydrolysis may be purely chemical or catalysed by enzymes. Digestion is normally achieved by enzyme-catalysed hydrolysis.
Concentrations of tryglycerides in the blood higher than normal (or reference) values.
Molecules which relay signals between cells of the immune system.
The accuracy of a study's findings with regard to the study subjects.
A reaction or study carried out in the living organism.
Chemical mediators of the inflammatory response, released by various white blood cells and by mast cells.
Expected further number of years of life measured at any age.
The channel within a tubular organ; for example, the lumen of the intestine.
A carotenoid found primarily in green leafy vegetables. Lutein has no provitamin A activity.
Forming connections of neurons at the epithelium.
Pertains to drug-like actions of chemical substances.
Activity which is demonstrated in various phases.
A carbohydrate polymer formed by the linking of many monosaccharides.
Concerning the relationships between measurable stimuli and the corresponding responses.
The totality of characteristics of an entity that bear on its ability to satisfy stated or implied needs.
The operational techniques and activities used to fulfil requirements for quality.
The organisational structure, procedures, processes and resources needed to implement quality management.
Fatty acid whose hydrocarbon chain contains no double bonds.
Fatty acids with chain lengths of two to six carbon atoms.

Precursor cell in various systems which is capable of producing the various functional cells of that system by cell division and differentiation, e.g., stem cells which differentiate into lymphocytes.
Preservatives commonly used in, for example, wine.
White blood cells involved in the immune response.T cells (T lymphocytes)
Triglyceride with a preponderance of unsaturated fatty acids.
The agent, such as a plasmid or virus, used to carry new DNA into a cell during genetic modification.

A ground tremor caused by the repositioning of rocks after an earthquake . Aftershocks may continue to occur for as long as two years after the initial earthquake. The intensity of an earth quake's aftershocks decreases over time.
Of or being an igneous rock containing grains that are so small as to be barely visible to the naked eye.
The section of a flood plain where deposits of fine silts and clays settle after a flood. Backswamps usually lie behind a stream's natural levees .
The lowest level to which a stream can erode the channel through which it flows, generally equal to the prevailing global sea level.

A massive discordant pluton with a surface area greater than 100 square kilometers, typically having a depth of about 30 kilometers. Batholiths are generally found in elongated mountain - ranges after the country rock above them has eroded.
The portion of a foreshore that lies nearest to the sea - and regularly receives the swash of breaking waves. The beach face is the steepest part of the foreshore.
A type of seismic wave that transmits energy from an earthquake's focus through the Earth's interior in all directions. See also surface wave .
A large, smooth, round or dome-shaped inselberg .
A bed made up of particles dropped from a moving cur- rent, as of wind or water, and marked by a downward slope that indicates the direction of the current that deposited them.
The set of processes that cause physical and chemical changes in sediment after it has been deposited and buried under another layer of sediment. Diagenesis may culminate in lithification .
The expansion of a rock's volume caused by stress and deformation .
1. The flow of a dry, highly viscous mass of clay-like or silty regolith, typically moving at a rate of one or two meters per hour. 2. The material that descends in such a flow.
The point on the Earth's surface that is located directly above the focus of an earthquake .

A minor, barely detectable earthquake, generally pre ceding a full-scale earthquake with approximately the same focus . Major quakes may follow a cluster of foreshocks by as little as a few seconds or as much as several weeks.
A steep ridge or hill left when a mountain has eroded and found in an otherwise flat, typically desert plain.

A large concordant pluton that is shaped like a dome or a mushroom. Laccoliths tend to form at relatively shallow depths and are typically composed of granite. The country rock above them often erodes away completely.
Water formed from the melted ice of a glacier .
A rock that incorporates both metamorphic and igneous materials.

A naturally occurring, usually inorganic, solid consisting of either a single element or a compound, and having a definite chemical composition but lacking a systemic internal arrangement of atoms. See also mineral .
A scientific law stating that all atoms, except those of hydrogen and helium, require eight electrons in the outermost energy level in order to maintain chemical stability.
A brown or black clastic source rock containing kerogen .

A crescent-shaped body of standing water formed from a single loop that was cut off from a meandering stream , typically by a flood that allowed the stream to flow through its flood plain and bypass the loop.
Of or being an igneous rock containing components large enough to be seen with the unaided eye.
A low ridge of sediment that forms along the inner bank of a meandering stream .
Sediment that sets off a sudden mudflow by changing rapidly from solid to liquid form, as after an earthquake, an explosion, or thunder
A series of events through which a rock changes, over time, between igneous , sedimentary and metamorphic forms.
A steep, isolated island of rock, separated from a head land by the action of waves, as when the overhanging section of a sea arch is eroded.
A visual record produced by a seismograph and showing the arrival times and magnitudes of various seismic waves .
The study of earthquakes and the structure of the Earth, based on data from seismic waves .
The boundary between a body of water and dry land. silica A compound consisting of silicon and oxygen.
The steep leeward slope of a dune .
A weak plane in a rock mass from which material is likely to break off in a slide .

A dune with three or four arms radiating from its usually higher center so that it resembles a star in shape. Star dunes form when winds blow from three or four directions, or when the wind direction shifts frequently.
The area running from the shoreline to the farthest point in the sea where waves begin to break.
A turbulent, abrupt, wall-like wave that is caused by a flood tide .
"The insoluble residue that derives from the anodic dissolution of an impure metal such as copper during electrorefining. Also called ""anode slime."" "
The electrolyte on the cathode side of an electrochemical cell that is divided into compartments.
"A series-coupled assembly of cells, a term used primarily in industrial electrolysis using electrolytic cells. "

"A miniature non-rechargeable battery, in the shape and size of a small coin used to power small electronic devices, e.g. watches and hearing aids. Also called ""button"" cell. See also an Encyclopedia Article. "

"A technique used in electroanalytical chemistry or in the determination of the kinetics and mechanism of electrode reactions, or a process carried out in an electrolytic cell that operates at constant current. See also chronopotentiometry. "

"Corrosion products are typically oxides, but other products (e.g., sulfides) can also form depending on the environment. Corrosion always involves oxidation of the corroding material in the general sense of the term. "
Instrument used for the measurement of electrical charge.
An electroanalytical technique based upon the measurement of the amount of electrical charge passed through the working electrode of an electrochemical cell.
The mobile ion in ion exchange. The ion with opposite charge to that of the fixed site on the ion-exchange resin. Contrast with fixed ion.
The permanently attached charged fragment in an ion-exchange resin. Contrast with counterion.
A concept similar to gram-mole except it relates to atoms rather than molecules.
An electrically conductive structural part that connects series-connected cells in a fuel cell stack.
"Instrument that can be used for the measurement of more than one parameter. Typically, it can be used to measure current, potential, and resistance. "
"10-9 ampere, symbol: ""nA"" (one billionth of an ampere). "
"The total ir drop in an electrochemical cell, including the ir drop in the solution between the electrodes and in any separator. "
The graphical representation of the result of polarography.
See electrode of the third kind.
"Measurement unit of electrical energy. Symbol: ""Wh"". Related units are that of energy density: watt-hour/kilogram (Wh/kg) and watt-hour/liter (Wh/l). "
A knob that allows you to scroll through Programs and change parameter values. Usually used when a keypad is not available or for fine tuning and scrolling through infinite variables.
The playing surface buttons which are designed into a drum machine and played with the fingers.
Allows instruments interconnected via MIDI to be synchronized. The MIDI Clock runs at a rate of 24 pulses-per-quarter- note.
The selectable MIDI echo function is used to provide an exact copy of any information recieved at the MIDI in port, and route this data directly to the MIDI out/echo port.
This port provides an exact copy of the incoming data at the MIDI in port and and transmits this data to another MIDI instrument or device that follows within the MIDI data chain.

A continuous controller which can be applied to synthesized note(s), usually from a joystick to the left of the lowest keyboard note. The sound is a raising or lowering of the pitch and changes as you move the joystick left and right.
When recording, punching out stops the recording process started by a punch in, thus preserving the previously recorded track starting at the punch out point.
The port on the back of the instrument to which SCSI devices are connected.
A sequencer mode where events are entered one at a time.
A substance that enhances the ability of a flux to remove oxides and other contaminants from surfaces being joined.
A via hole extending only to one surface of a printed circuit board.
A void caused by outgassing. (Outgassing is a gaseous emission from a printed circuit assembly when exposed to a reduced pressure or heat or both.
(Process Capability Index) Ability to meet a customer's specification. A measure of the relationship between the scaled distance between the process mean value and the closest specification limit.
A component placement term measuring machine speed from pickup to board location and return. Also called the test rate.

A situation where a lead or pad was at one point in the soldering process wetted by the solder, but due to extended time or temperature, the presence of intermetallics, volatiles or other causes, has become withdrawn from the wetted surface.
The placement machine for chips in a chip-on-board process line.

Equipment that picks die from a wafer and presents them for their next process step. When used in reference to bare die placement machines, the die are presented for pick by the machine's placement nozzles.
A connector for a Dual In-Line Package, or one that has its leads in two parallel rows.

Surface mount components with a lead pitch of at least 50 mils. Fine pitch is more commonly used to refer to components with a lead pitch of 25 mils or less. These packages usually require vision assistance for accurate placement.

An integrated circuit package with leads on two or four sides. The leads on these packages are either gull wing or flat, and have standard spacing. Packages with a lead pitch below 50 mils are referred to as fine pitch packages.
A device on a stencil-printing system that drags solderpaste back to the starting point after the squeegee has made a printing stroke.
The angle of the lead foot after lead forming with respect to the plane defined by the bottom of the component.
A component or assembly tested and known to function to spec, then used to test other units via comparison.
The opening in TAB tape where the innermost extremities of the lead are bonded to the IC.
The innermost portion of the lead on a TAB tape site that extends into the ILB window.

A strip of polyimide between the inner and outer lead bonding areas on a TAB tape site. This strip typically encircles the entire IC. It is a common feature in many TAB tape designs, but is not found in all cases.
A class of materials that do not conduct electricity and are characterized by high resistivity.
The width of the lead in a defined area of a component.
The angle of the vertical portion of a lead with respect to a plane perpendicular to the plane defined by the bottom of the component.
The part of the component lead between the two bend radii. The leg length is directly related to the overall lead form height.
Plastic debris remaining on a plastic molded package after the component manufacturing process. This can occur on molded carrier ring (MCR) and plastic quad pack (PQFP) components.
Tape that sliced silicon wafers are placed on prior to dicing.
An opening in TAB tape that the outer leads span. Typically, this opening is where outer leads are excised from the tape.

An instrument that measures ionic residues on PCB surfaces via immersion of an assembly into a water-alcohol mixture of a known high resistivity, after which a drop in resistivity due to ionic residue over time is measured and recorded.
The length of lead that extends across the OLB window. It is typically excised, formed, and attached to a substrate.
The gaseous emission or de-aeration from a PCB or solder joint.
Planarity refers to substrate surface flatness. It is another term for board warpage.
A nonconductive polymer used as base material for two and three layer TAB tape .
Thermosetting ring chain polymers characterized by -NH group. They are being increasingly used as dielectrics in high performance circuits.
A resin and small amounts of organic activators in an organic solvent.
Rosin in an organic solvent or rosin as a paste with activators.
An alkaline chemical added to water to improve its ability to dissolve rosin flux residues.
A printed circuit board deemed to be suitable for determining the acceptability of a group of boards produced with the same fabrication process.

Contact points on TAB tape, located outside the OLB window, that are used to facilitate testing and burn-in of the IC while it is in the TAB frame. Test pads remain with the discarded portion of the carrier after excising.
A specific point of access to an electrical circuit used for electrical testing purposes.

In flip chip applications, the material injected under the die after testing to ensure reliability. This material is particularly important for flip chips mounted on substrates with different CTEs than silicon, such as FR-4 and some ceramics.

[Hindu] A form of the Hindu god Vishnu.
